sources.entry: A gallery is software that helps the user publish or share photos, pictures, videos or other digital media.

summary.name: Gallery software
summary.one_liner: Gallery software is a category of programs that lets users publish or share photos, pictures, videos and other digital media, usually on web servers.
summary.what_it_does: This Wikipedia page is a general overview of gallery software, which helps users publish or share photos, pictures, videos and other digital media. It notes that most galleries run on web servers where users can register and upload. Typical features named are automatic image resizing, grouping media into sets or albums, and comments. The page distinguishes managed galleries, where an administrator controls albums (examples given: Coppermine and Gallery Project), from decentralised ones without a central administrator, such as MediaGoblin, where each user creates their own collections. It also covers early imageboards like Futallaby and Danbooru.
notable: Distinguishes managed galleries (admin-controlled albums) from decentralised galleries (per-user collections)
Covers imageboards such as Futallaby and Danbooru as early media-sharing software
Names open source examples: Coppermine, Gallery Project, MediaGoblin
caveats: Page is a general encyclopedia overview of a software category, not a single product, so no pricing or licensing for a specific tool is given
